quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to start moving.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What formation should a motorcycle group use?

options.text: Always single-file.
It depends on the situation.
Always staggered.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for groups. Switch to single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering highways, or leaving highways.

questions.question: As your motorcycle speeds up, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a higher gear.
Shift to a lower gear.
Put the bike in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a higher gear.
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle speeds up, shift into higher gears.

questions.question: How do you shift to a higher gear?

options.text: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift.
Place your foot over the shift lever and push.
Use your thumb to move the lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift.
questions.explanation: To shift to a higher gear, put your foot under the shift lever and lift it.

questions.question: What clothing should you wear while riding?

options.text: Bright clothing.
Dark clothing.
Uncomfortable clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to be more visible when riding, even during the day. Reflective materials also help.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must stop completely, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should all riders do?

options.text: Keep safe distance from each other.
Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep safe distance from each other.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay together while keeping safe distances from each other.

questions.question: What happens as your motorcycle speeds up?

options.text: You need to shift up through the gears.
You need to shift down through the gears.
You need to put it in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: You need to shift up through the gears.
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle goes faster, shift into higher gears.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride a little faster than normal.
Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, making it slower to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing earlier, reduce your speed, and look for larger gaps when crossing or merging into traffic.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have time to react to hazards.
You have space to maneuver.
You have more time to speed up when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to speed up when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time to react and room to maneuver if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: Only a few minutes.
About an hour.
It should only be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only a few minutes.
questions.explanation: You should inspect your motorcycle before every ride. This inspection only takes a few minutes.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: Only at night.
Only during the day.
Both day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing at all times when riding, whether it is day or night.

questions.question: What danger does long-term wind noise exposure pose?

options.text: It is not dangerous.
It can cause permanent hearing damage.
It is just part of riding a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause permanent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear protection when riding. Good ear protection lets you hear important sounds like sirens and car horns.

questions.question: How can you best avoid fatigue on a long motorcycle trip?

options.text: Take frequent breaks to rest.
Ride as fast as possible.
Take artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent breaks to rest.
questions.explanation: Limit your daily riding time and take frequent rest breaks to avoid fatigue. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may crash from extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: What should you look for when scanning around your motorcycle?

options.text: Possible escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
Whether you can travel faster than other vehicles.
Pedestrians to stare at.

questions.correctAnswerText: Possible escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
questions.explanation: Search the road for hazards and look for escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-compliant helmet?

options.text: It severely limits your vision.
It allows you to see enough to the sides for safe riding.
It can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see as far as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do when other vehicles are stopped or moving slowly?

options.text: Do not weave between lanes of traffic.
It is okay to weave in and out of traffic lanes.
Ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Do not ride between rows of stopped or slow vehicles. Vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or people may stick arms out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to stay safe.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of proper lane positioning?

options.text: Increases your ability to be seen.
Helps you avoid surface hazards.
Invites other road users into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invites other road users into your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane positioning helps you be seen and avoid hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What usually causes a "wobble" or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
Improper tightening of the front wheel to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
questions.explanation: A wobble is sudden shaking of the front wheel and handlebars. It is usually caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What does the SEE strategy stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding decisions. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, a motorcyclist:

options.text: May stay in the same lane as the other vehicle.
Must use a clear lane.
Can ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must use a clear lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcyclist cannot pass another vehicle in the same lane. Sharing a lane while passing is dangerous and not allowed.

questions.question: During a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean the same way.
The motorcycle and rider should lean opposite ways.
The motorcycle should not lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean the same way.
questions.explanation: In a normal turn, the rider and motorcycle lean together in the same direction. In a slow, tight turn, the motorcycle leans while the rider keeps their body more upright to balance.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, there is usually an oily strip. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease buildup.
Not worry about the oil and grease buildup.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease buildup.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease buildup.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease buildup. The oily strip in the center of a lane is usually only about two feet wide, so you can often stay to the left or right side and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, a motorcyclist should stay at least this far behind the vehicle ahead:

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second gap between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Use a larger gap if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: If parked vehicles are on your right and no traffic is coming toward you, you should ride:

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked vehicles on your right with no oncoming traffic. This helps you avoid dangers like opening car doors and pedestrians stepping out. If oncoming traffic is present, stay in the center of your lane for more space around you.

questions.question: A good defensive rider:

options.text: Always travels slowly.
Watches what other drivers do.
Travels at the same speed at all times.
Only rides in areas they know well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: A defensive rider watches other road users and prepares for problems. Even experienced riders get distracted. Being defensive makes you more alert and ready for anything.

questions.question: How should you brake?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located?

options.text: By the left footrest.
By the right footrest.
By the right handle grip.

questions.correctAnswerText: By the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest and is operated by the rider's left foot.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Only stop if other traffic is coming.
Vehicles will enter the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, let all traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane ends.
